name: Dabigatran etexilate
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Dabigatran is a direct thrombin inhibitor cleared about 80% by the kidneys, so exposure rises steeply as kidney function falls (AUC 3.2-fold at CrCl 30–50 and 6.3-fold at 15–30). The US label uses 150 mg twice daily above CrCl 30 and 75 mg twice daily at 15–30 for atrial fibrillation, and gives no dose below 15 or on dialysis. For venous thromboembolism it gives no dose at CrCl 30 or below. It is dialyzable.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses Cockcroft-Gault CrCl (mL/min): >30, 15–30, <15; P-gp inhibitor limits at 30–50 and <50.

bands.recommendation: Atrial fibrillation (AF): 150 mg twice daily. VTE treatment or prevention of recurrence: 150 mg twice daily (after 5 to 10 days of parenteral anticoagulation for treatment). Hip-replacement prophylaxis: 110 mg on day 1, then 220 mg once daily (label).
CrCl >30: usual doses. With P-gp inhibitors: AF at CrCl 30–50 with dronedarone or systemic ketoconazole, 75 mg twice daily; VTE indications at CrCl <50, avoid P-gp inhibitors (label).

AF, CrCl 15–30: 75 mg twice daily; avoid P-gp inhibitors (label). VTE indications at CrCl ≤30: dosing cannot be provided. This dose is based on pharmacokinetic modeling; CrCl <30 was not studied in RE-LY (label 12.3). PH registers 75 mg capsules.
bands.short: AF 75 mg BID; VTE: no dose

bands.recommendation: AF at CrCl <15: dosing recommendations cannot be provided (label). Site position (not label wording): avoid; exposure rises steeply (AUC 6.3-fold at CrCl 15–30, label 12.3), and in hemodialysis patients with AF dabigatran was associated with more bleeding than warfarin (Chan 2015). Choose another anticoagulant.
bands.short: Avoid: no dose; more bleeding on HD

hd.text: Dosing recommendations cannot be provided (label): CrCl <15 or dialysis for atrial fibrillation; CrCl ≤30 or dialysis for VTE treatment, prevention of recurrence and hip-replacement prophylaxis. Hemodialysis removes about 49% to 57% over 4 hours (label 10). In hemodialysis patients with AF, dabigatran was associated with more hospitalization or death from bleeding than warfarin (rate ratio 1.48) and more hemorrhagic death (rate ratio 1.78) (Chan 2015); choose another anticoagulant. The red tile is a site position, not label wording.
hd.short: Avoid: no dose; more bleeding on HD

pd.text: No dose in label (dialysis): dosing recommendations cannot be provided. Site position (not label wording): avoid, as on hemodialysis (Chan 2015); choose another anticoagulant.
pd.short: Avoid: no dose; more bleeding on HD

crrt.text: No dose in label. Site position (not label wording): avoid; exposure rises steeply as kidney function falls (label 12.3). Use another anticoagulant.
crrt.short: Avoid: no dose; more bleeding on HD

dialyzable: Yes: high-flux hemodialysis removed about 49% over 4 hours (blood flow 200 mL/min) to 57% (300 mL/min), with 7% to 15% rebound; protein binding about 35% (label 10).
monitoring: CrCl before starting and when kidney function may decline (e.g., hypovolemia, nephrotoxic drugs); stop if acute kidney injury. Bleeding, hemoglobin. Reversal: idarucizumab in adults; hemodialysis has limited supporting data. Before surgery or invasive procedures, stop 1 to 2 days ahead if CrCl ≥50 mL/min, 3 to 5 days if CrCl <50; longer for major surgery or spinal/epidural procedures (label 2.8).

pediatric.approved_ages: VTE treatment and prevention of recurrence, 8 to <18 years (capsules); other dabigatran dosage forms for under 8 years (label).
pediatric.usual_dose: Weight-based twice daily (label Table 1): 11 to <16 kg, 75 mg; 16 to <26 kg, 110 mg; 26 to <41 kg, 150 mg; 41 to <61 kg, 185 mg; 61 to <81 kg, 220 mg; 81 kg or more, 260 mg.
pediatric.max_dose: 260 mg twice daily (81 kg or more).
pediatric.egfr_equation: Bedside Schwartz: eGFR = 0.413 × height (cm) / serum creatinine (mg/dL) (label 2.4).

renal.recommendation: eGFR >50: weight-based dose. eGFR <50: avoid (no data, higher exposure; label 2.4).

sources.citation: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharmaceuticals Inc. (2025). PRADAXA (dabigatran etexilate) capsules [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA022512, set ID ba74e3cd-b06f-4145-b284-5fd6b84ff3c9, version effective June 25, 2025]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

Schwartz, G. J., Muñoz, A., Schneider, M. F., Mak, R. H., Kaskel, F., Warady, B. A., & Furth, S. L. (2009). New equations to estimate GFR in children with CKD. Journal of the American Society of Nephrology, 20(3), 629–637.
Chan, K. E., Edelman, E. R., Wenger, J. B., Thadhani, R. I., & Maddux, F. W. (2015). Dabigatran and rivaroxaban use in atrial fibrillation patients on hemodialysis. Circulation, 131(11), 972–979.

adult: JUDGMENT: CrCl <15, HD, PD and CRRT tiles are gray ('no label dose') per the color rule; Dr. Rivero may prefer red ('avoid') given ~80% renal clearance.

PH registers 75, 110 and 150 mg capsules. In the US label 110 mg is used only for hip-replacement prophylaxis (and pediatric tiers); 110 mg twice daily for AF (studied in RE-LY) is not a US-approved dose.
'Alternative anticoagulant usually chosen' at CrCl <15 is clinical judgment, labelled as such.

revision_log.change: CrCl <15, HD, PD and CRRT tiles changed to red as a site position (label PK plus Chan 2015: bleeding RR 1.48, hemorrhagic death RR 1.78); label sentence 'dosing recommendations cannot be provided' kept.
Pre-procedure stop times from label 2.8 added to monitoring (1–2 days CrCl ≥50; 3–5 days CrCl <50; longer for major surgery or neuraxial procedures).
CrCl 15–29: 75 mg dose is from PK modeling; CrCl <30 not studied in RE-LY (label 12.3).
